newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: PLO "astonished" Romanian flew to Jerusalem airport.
newsitem.headline: PLO "astonished" Romanian flew to Jerusalem airport.

text.p: The Palestine Liberation Organisation's U.N. observer expressed astonishment on Tuesday that Romania's foreign minister flew into an airport north of Jerusalem, in an area captured by Israel in the 1967 war, during a recent visit to Israel.
Most visitors to Israel fly in to Ben Gurion airport, near Tel Aviv.

"We were astonished by an action taken by a member state ... which is obviously in violation of Security Council resolutions and resolutions of ICAO (the International Civil Aviation Organisation) on Jerusalem ...," Nasser Al-Kidwa told a meeting of the U.N. committee on Palestinian rights.
He said the Romanian official, Adrian Severin, had used the airport on a visit last month. Al-Kidwa noted that Romania was a member of the U.N. Palestine rights committee.

Al-Kidwa also said an emergency special session of the General Assembly on Israeli settlements should be resumed quickly following the recent publication of a report by Secretary-General Kofi Annan saying Israel had not abandoned its construction of a new settlement in occupied territory south of Jerusalem.

The assembly, at an emergency session in April, adopted a resolution demanding an immediate halt to the building of an Israeli housing project at the site, called Har Homa in Hebrew and Jabal Abu Ghneim in Arabic, and an end to all support for "illegal Israeli activities" in the occupied territories.

Al-Kidwa said the Arab group of states would request a resumption of the assembly session and that a date around July 15 would be the most appropriate time. The group also was working on a resolution that should be stronger than the one adopted in April, he added.

Citing possible elements of such a draft, he said it should deal with "support given by the private sector to the illegal Israeli settlement activities." He noted that Annan's report mentioned a hotel franchised by a United States-based chain in an Israeli settlement in the Gaza Strip.

Hinting at a move to bar Israel from the assembly, he said: "The normal participation of member states in the work of the General Assembly cannot take place on the basis of total violation of international law and relevant Security Council resolutions, as well as total disregard of the will of the international community."
